title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Accounting earnings can be sculpted by a single tax ruling or inventory build; ten-year free cash flow and return on invested capital never lie.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Principle

web_blocks.html: A 10-year review from FY2017 to FY2026 shows Qualcomm's full cycle. FY2017–FY2020 brought flat sales and legal fines, including a -$4.96B GAAP net loss in FY2018 [17, 18]. Next came the FY2021–FY2022 5G boom, lifting sales to $44.20B and operating income to $15.86B [17]. An inventory glut hit FY2023 ($35.82B sales) before diversification lifted FY2026 revenue back to $43.12B [17, 18].

web_blocks.caption: Table 6.1: Qualcomm 10-Year Financial Forensics (FY2017–FY2026, $ Billions)
web_blocks.takeaway: Qualcomm doubled sales from $22.3B to $43.1B over ten years and earned ~$76.2B in total FCF. FY2026 FCF-to-Net-Income fell to 63% due to a $4.21B tax benefit and a $2.11B inventory build.

web_blocks.html: Forensic readers should look past FY2026's headline net income jump. GAAP Net Income rose to $13.63 billion even though operating income fell 30% from $12.36 billion to $8.66 billion [2, 3]. That gap came from an $11.3 billion tax swing. In Q4 FY2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB) triggered a $5.7 billion federal deferred tax valuation allowance ($7.12 billion GAAP tax expense). Qualcomm reversed that reserve in Q2 FY2026 after IRS Notice 2026-07 allowed capitalized R&D to offset CAMT, creating a $5.7 billion non-cash gain ($4.21 billion net tax benefit; FY2026 Form 10-K, Note 3) [2, 3]. Actual cash taxes paid in FY2026 were $1,644 million, down from $3.1 billion in FY2025. The balance sheet also carries a $2.7 billion Korean withholding tax receivable against $3.0 billion in unrecognized tax benefits, exposed to $271 million per 10% KRW swing (Note 3). Stripping out the one-time tax benefit and $3.45 billion in Stock-Based Compensation puts true economic Free Cash Flow near $5.2 billion [3].

Balance-sheet health remains investment-grade, though capital returns exceeded FCF and gross debt rose post-cutoff. Audited FY2026 cash flows (Form 10-K, F-6 & Exhibit 99.1) show $7,817 million in share repurchases (48 million shares) and $3,854 million in dividends [2, 3]. That $11,671 million total equaled 134.9% of $8,651 million FCF, alongside $1,134 million in employee RSU tax-withholding cash outlays [2, 3]. Cash and marketable securities fell from $10,155 million (plus $2,323 million restricted cash) to $7,681 million ($4,636M cash plus $3,045M securities). Total FY2026 debt stood at $15,112 million ($2,492M short-term including $499M commercial paper and $1,993M 2027 notes, plus $12,620M long-term), leaving ~$7.43 billion in net debt [1, 3]. Post-cutoff, on November 12, 2026 (Form 8-K filed Nov 13, 2026; 424B5), Qualcomm issued $4.00 billion of 5.000%–5.800% senior unsecured notes due 2028–2036 (~$3.98 billion net proceeds). Proceeds will retire the 3.250% 2027 notes and boost liquidity, lifting pro forma cash to $9,661 million and pro forma debt to $17,098 million (~$7.44 billion net debt at higher coupons). Meanwhile, FY2026 M&A (Alphawave, Modular, and 8 bolt-ons) lifted Goodwill +44.2% to $16,374 million (26.9% of $60,829 million assets; $4,353 million in Data Center/Nonreportable). Total equity stood at $30,401 million with a 1.86x current ratio.

web_blocks.caption: Table 6.2: Capital Return, SBC Dilution & Return on Capital Forensics (FY2025–FY2026)
rows: Exceptionally high vs. ~9%–10% WACC, though goodwill surged +44.2% to $16.37B on $6.0B FY26 M&A [Blind Snapshot].
Audited FY26 buybacks consumed 90.4% of FCF ($8,651M); offset by 46M shares issued ($4,512M M&A + RSUs) (FY2026 Form 10-K, F-6 & Note 4).
Total FY26 capital return of $11,671M = 134.9% of FCF; 5.3% 3Y / 6.4% 5Y dividend CAGR (FY2026 Form 10-K, F-6) [Blind Snapshot].
Up +24% YoY; plus $1,134M RSU tax-withholding cash outflow, $4.1B unrecognized RSU backlog (1.9 yrs), and $635M M&A retention comp (Note 5).
Ending shares fell just -0.2% (1,074M to 1,072M) as M&A/RSUs offset buybacks; 25M-share AWS warrant adds ~2.3% potential overhang (Note 4).
web_blocks.takeaway: Qualcomm's 31.1% ROIC remains elite, yet audited FY2026 filings show $11.67B of capital return (135% of FCF) barely shrank ending shares (-0.2% to 1,072M). Issuing 46M shares for M&A and RSUs offset buybacks, leaving $4.1B in unrecognized RSU cost plus a 25M-share AWS warrant.

web_blocks.mechanism: Leveraged fabless-era semiconductor complexity and high-ROIC installed-base services to dampen hardware cyclicality, while returning >90% of Free Cash Flow via buybacks and dividends.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Compounded revenue from $9.7B (FY15) to >$27B (FY24–25) while shrinking diluted share count by ~30% and sustaining >25% ROIC across two memory/logic downturns.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: High-ROIC chip firms pairing cyclical hardware with recurring IP can compound per-share FCF across cycles. That works only if buybacks are not masked by rising SBC or peak inventory builds.

book_paragraphs: When you and I pull back the camera to look at ten full years of Qualcomm's audited financials, from fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2026, two things jump off the page immediately. First, this business has doubled in scale—from $22.3 billion in revenue to $43.1 billion—while generating roughly $76 billion in cumulative Free Cash Flow without owning a single wafer fab. Second, it is unmistakably cyclical. Look at the rhythm: the 2018 regulatory and Apple storm pushed operating margins down to 2.7% and produced a $4.96 billion GAAP net loss; the 2022 5G super-cycle propelled operating income to a record $15.86 billion at a 35.9% margin; the 2023 smartphone inventory glut knocked operating income in half to $7.79 billion; and fiscal 2026 sits at $8.66 billion in GAAP operating profit while the business digests Apple's modem exit and invests heavily for data centers.

Why did fiscal 2026 GAAP Net Income jump to $13.63 billion even while operating income fell 30% from $12.36 billion to $8.66 billion? That is exactly why we do forensic accounting instead of reading headline EPS. In Q4 FY2025, U.S. tax reform under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act forced Qualcomm to record a $5.7 billion valuation allowance on federal deferred tax assets ($7.12 billion GAAP tax expense); then in Q2 FY2026, IRS Notice 2026-07 allowed capitalized R&D to reduce Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax, letting Qualcomm reverse that $5.7 billion allowance into a $4.21 billion net income tax benefit. Actual cash income taxes paid in FY2026 were $1,644 million (down from $3.1 billion in FY2025), while the balance sheet still carries a $2.7 billion Korean withholding tax receivable against $3.0 billion in unrecognized tax benefits exposed to Korean won swings. Meanwhile, cash flow from operations fell from $14.01 billion to $11.15 billion because inventory swelled by $2.11 billion, and capital expenditures more than doubled to $2.49 billion. Free Cash Flow landed at $8.65 billion—still a healthy 20.1% of sales, just without the artificial glow of the tax reversal.

Turn to the balance sheet and you see an investment-grade franchise that leaned harder into debt and goodwill during 2026. Qualcomm closed fiscal 2026 on September 27 with $7.68 billion in cash and marketable securities against $15.11 billion in debt (roughly $7.43 billion net debt), while Goodwill jumped 44% in a single year to $16.37 billion—nearly 27% of total assets—after $6.0 billion of data-center and AI acquisitions. Then, in mid-November 2026 (Form 8-K filed November 13), Qualcomm tapped the bond market for $4.00 billion in new 5.00% to 5.80% senior notes maturing between 2028 and 2036 to refinance $2.0 billion of 3.25% 2027 notes and pad corporate cash, lifting pro forma cash to $9.66 billion and pro forma gross debt to $17.10 billion at higher coupon costs. Return on Invested Capital sits at 31.1%, clearing a ~9% to 10% cost of capital by more than twenty percentage points.

There is, however, one forensic reality you should never gloss over: Stock-Based Compensation and acquisition equity dilution. In fiscal 2026, Qualcomm spent an audited $7.82 billion repurchasing 48 million shares and paid $3.85 billion in dividends—returning $11.67 billion to owners, or 135% of Free Cash Flow—plus another $1.13 billion in cash tax withholdings on vesting employee RSUs. Yet ending shares outstanding barely budged, slipping just 0.2% from 1,074 million to 1,072 million, because Qualcomm issued 46 million new shares for the Alphawave and Modular acquisitions ($4.51 billion in stock) and employee grants. With GAAP SBC up 24% to $3.45 billion (8% of sales), $4.1 billion of unrecognized RSU expense still sitting in the pipeline over the next 1.9 years, $635 million in executive retention stock tied to Alphawave and Modular, and a 25-million-share AWS warrant overhanging the data center ramp (alongside routine Rule 10b5-1 executive share sales in November 2026), true economic Free Cash Flow after SBC is closer to $5.2 billion than $8.65 billion.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Qualcomm's 31.1% ROIC and ~$76B in 10-year FCF confirm an elite asset-light core, but FY2026's $5.7B CAMT tax release, $3.45B SBC ($4.1B unvested backlog), 46M new shares issued against 48M repurchased, $16.37B goodwill, and $17.10B pro forma debt remind us to underwrite on SBC-adjusted FCF and per-share net dilution rather than headline GAAP net income.
